Taste Library

Grid:

131 award-winning websites, read as one system of 43 families.

Agents swept every Awwwards Site of the Year and Site of the Month winner from 2018-2026, opened each one, and wrote down what it actually does. Not a gallery — a taxonomy, with the working shown.

Every figure on this page is generated from the dataset. None is typed by hand.

The method

  1. HarvestCrawl the archives. 131 rows kept at 2018+, each with its award, date and live URL.
  2. CardOne study card per site, written from the case page and the live build, then attacked by a second agent that had to disprove it.
  3. ClusterTwo independent agents proposed taxonomies; a third reconciled them. 43 families survived.
  4. DissectPer family, a deep dive: prose reference plus original re-implementations of the signature techniques.
  5. ValidateEvery constant re-checked for whether it takes effect — not just whether it was copied correctly.
  6. CompileThe survivors became a skill an agent can use to design from, citing sources.

What the checking found

The interesting part is not the taxonomy. It is that the code we wrote about other people's code was the least reliable thing in the library.

A late pass re-read every extracted constant asking a question the earlier passes never had: does this value actually do anything? 1,112 defects came back. 37 of the sites studied are themselves already offline — the awarded design gone, even where the domain still answers.

Nothing was deleted. Defects are annotated where they sit, because a record of what was wrong is worth more than a clean file that lies.

43 families

Ordered by member count. Each is a visual system, not a template — the Not for line is the part that keeps it honest.

01

matte-toybox-playworld

A full-bleed matte 3D toy world you inhabit — walk, drive, fly at eye level instead of scrolling — hue and silhouette separating objects, candy grading per zone, UI shrunk to a white sticker layer.

Members
9
Live
4
Temperature
Candy over cool fog #93a2bf: sky #81BFBC, ink #363a3c, accent #66BDE6, #f3c258 #c25959
Type
Physical type: extruded 3D letters in-scene; MSDF in-world copy (UglyDave-Alternates dialogue, REM-Medium nametags)
Motion
Mostly linear — 'none' 69x vs inOut1 11x; physics carries the feel. House eases: inOut1 cubic-bezier(.5,0,.1,1), inOut2 (.56,0,0,1).
Varies by
Traversal agency vs surviving chrome: Bruno's physics car, zero chrome → Messenger in-canvas UI → Kode diorama-menu → Oat watch-and-choose

For Brief is 'a world exists and you should want to be in it' with a real loop — play, explore, role-play — to justify traversal replacing scroll.

Not for Pastiche when content needs SEO/a11y/deep-links/conversion (empty-DOM trade); a game-skin with no playable loop; multiplayer as decoration; real content on a walkable sphere — no URLs, no back button.

blackbox-keyline-hud

No document: a black full-viewport canvas stage where emissive content is the only light, the interface is hairline HUD keylines in tracked micro-caps, and navigation is camera travel.

Live
2

Type
NB Architekt: tracked micro-caps 9–15px / 0.1em for all labels + one 110px hairline display cut; nothing mid-size
Motion
